sons.seo: Sleep Sounds With No Ads: Rain Sounds, Waves and Forests
sons.desc: Sleep sounds with no ads: rain, ocean waves, forest streams, flutes and soft drones on a 5 to 60 minute timer. A gentler alternative to white noise, offline.
sons.h1: Sleep sounds with no ads: rain sounds, ocean waves, flutes and soft drones
sons.lead: The sleep sounds in MeditaDream are made for winding down at the end of the day. There are thirteen of them, in three families, from rain and ocean waves to flutes and soft drones. The nature sounds are real recordings, made in forests, beside a Highland stream and by the ocean. You can play any of them on its own, with a timer that fades out gently. During a guided meditation, you can also play one softly under the voice. Like everything in the app, the sounds come with no subscription, no ads and no account.

sections.h2: Rain sounds for sleep and other nature sounds
p: The nature family brings together five real recordings. After Rain combines falling rain with the sounds of a tropical forest. Ocean Waves is the sound of the ocean, wave after wave. Highland Stream carries the steady flow of a stream in the Scottish Highlands.

Two forests complete the family. Woodland was recorded in a forest in the Netherlands, alive with birds. Northwoods takes you to a vast northern forest full of birdsong. If you are looking for rain sounds for sleep, start with After Rain, then try Ocean Waves on another evening.

sections.h2: Meditation music: flutes, a singing bowl and throat singing
p: The second family, instruments and voices, is closer to meditation music. Resonance is a singing bowl that sounds once every four minutes. Chinese Flute features the dizi, a traditional Chinese flute. Xiao brings back the xiao flute every five minutes.

Khoomei is overtone throat singing, in which a single voice produces two notes at once. Fairy Tale plays classic fairy-tale themes. Choose this family when silence feels too empty but words feel like too much. These sounds can also keep you company while you read, stretch or simply rest.
The third family is the most minimal. Nebula is a soft, spacious soundscape with a cosmic feel. Monolith is a deep drone built on low subharmonics, for when you want a sound to sink into.

Theta uses binaural beats. Each ear hears a slightly different tone, and the 4 Hz gap between them falls in the theta range. That is why Theta needs headphones: each ear must hear its own tone. Nothing here promises a particular effect, so take Theta simply as a sound, and keep it if you like it.

sections.h2: A sleep sounds timer that fades out on its own
p: Timed Ambience plays a single sound, with no voice, for the length of time you pick: from 5 minutes to an hour. At the end, the sound fades out over six seconds, then stops. Locking the screen does not interrupt it, so you can put your phone down and close your eyes.
The timer is handy beyond bedtime too. Try ten minutes of Woodland during a break, or half an hour of Highland Stream while you read.

MeditaDream has no synthetic white noise. Instead, it offers real recordings of rain, waves and running water: After Rain, Ocean Waves and Highland Stream. A recording keeps the small irregularities of a real place, while white noise sounds the same from one moment to the next.
If you would rather have a sound without water, Nebula is a soft cosmic soundscape. If you usually listen to white noise at night, these are good places to start.

sections.h2: How to use sleep sounds at bedtime
p: At night, a sleep sounds app should never interrupt you with an ad or a login screen. MeditaDream has neither, so the sound simply plays. A few habits can make it even more pleasant:
ul: Keep the volume low, just loud enough to hear.
Use headphones for Theta. The other sounds play well through your phone's speaker.
Pick a timer length close to the time you usually need to drift off.
Choose a continuous sound, such as Highland Stream, if you prefer nothing to change. Resonance and Xiao come back at intervals.
Give one sound a few evenings before you switch to another.

faq: Is this sleep sounds app really free?
Yes, completely: no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases and no account. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play.
Do I need headphones?
Only for Theta, because its binaural beats need each ear to hear its own tone. All the other sounds work through the phone's speaker.
Can I hear these sounds during a meditation?
Yes. During a guided meditation, tap “Background sound” in the player to play one softly under the voice. Each immersive world also has its own ambience, and Timed Ambience plays a sound on its own.
Which sound should I try first?
If you like rain sounds for sleep, start with After Rain. If you prefer music, try Chinese Flute or Fairy Tale, then compare them over a few evenings.

gratitude.seo: Free Gratitude Journal App with Guided Gratitude Meditations
gratitude.desc: A free gratitude journal app with eleven sections, plus guided gratitude meditations. No subscription, no ads, no account, works offline.
gratitude.h1: A free gratitude journal app: notice the good, one line at a time
gratitude.lead: A gratitude journal is a small ritual: each day, you write down a few things you are grateful for. In MeditaDream, the Gratitude & Growth journal gives this ritual a home, with eleven sections and guided gratitude meditations to go with it. Everything you write stays on your phone. The app is free, with no subscription, no ads and no account.

p: A gratitude journal is a notebook for the good things in your life, big or small. You might note a kind word, a good meal or a quiet moment in the sun. Writing them down is a way to slow down and really notice them.

There is nothing to perform and nothing to prove. The journal simply invites you to look at your day from a slightly different angle, and to keep a trace of what went well. On a hard day, one small thing is enough.
Gratitude does not mean pretending that everything is fine. It sits next to the rest of your day, without erasing it.

sections.h2: How to keep a gratitude journal, simply
p: The simplest method is often the one you will keep. There is no right length and no perfect moment, only a rhythm that suits you. Here are a few ideas to get started:
ul: Write one to three things a day. A single line is enough.
Be specific: name the exact moment, like a message from a friend or the smell of rain.
Pick a regular time, such as bedtime or your morning coffee.
Include yourself now and then: something you did well also counts.
Think of people too, and what they brought to your day.
Keep it private. It is easier to be honest when no one else will read it.
If you miss a day, simply start again the next one.

p: The Gratitude & Growth journal is made for what you are grateful for, and for where you want to grow. Daily Gratitude is the natural place to start.
You do not need to use every section. Daily Gratitude alone can carry the habit for a long time, and the others wait for the days when you want to explore further.

Some sections stay close to gratitude itself, such as Self Gratitude or Relationship Gratitude. Others turn toward growth, like Emotional Growth or Growth Tracker. Self Discovery and Forgiveness Practice go deeper, for evenings when you have more time. Here are all eleven:
ul: Daily Gratitude
Self Gratitude
Relationship Gratitude
Emotional Growth
Evolution, Confidence & Self-Worth
Spiritual Growth
Micro Victories
Growth Tracker
Gratitude through Life
Self Discovery
Forgiveness Practice

sections.h2: Gratitude meditation, from the body to the people who matter
p: Daily Gratitude is also the name of a 14-minute guided session. It begins in the body, with simple thanks for your legs, your sense of taste and your breath.

Precise Gratitude takes only 3 minutes: you pick one particular thing you truly value and rest your whole attention on it. For a longer gratitude meditation, try Gratitude to Your Guides, which lasts 23 minutes. It is a chance to thank, in turn, the people who have counted in your life, even those you never met. Two more sessions, on self-love and compassion, complete the selection.

sections.h2: A gratitude journal app that stays on your phone
p: Your journal is personal. Everything you write stays on your phone, and there is no account to create. With no ads and no subscription, nothing interrupts the moment you take for yourself.
The guided meditations download once, then play offline. Alongside Gratitude & Growth, the app includes four other journals, such as the Dream Journal and the Emotional Journal.
If you want a routine, pair the journal with a short gratitude meditation. It only takes a few minutes:
ul: Listen to Precise Gratitude, which lasts 3 minutes.
In the journal, go to Daily Gratitude and write one line.
Read it back once, slowly, before you put your phone away.
On busy evenings, keep only the first step: three minutes is enough.

faq: Is this gratitude journal app free?
Yes. It is completely free, with no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases and no account. It is available on the App Store and Google Play.
Who can read my journal?
Your entries stay on your phone, and there is no account to sign in to. The journal is yours alone.
How much should I write each day?
A line or two is enough. What matters is noticing something real, not filling a page.
What is the difference between the journal and a gratitude meditation?
The journal is for writing, while the meditations are guided listening sessions. You can pair them: a short meditation first, then a few lines in the journal.

oracle.seo: The Oracle: Three Guided Meditations for How You Feel
oracle.desc: Type how you feel and the Oracle turns over three cards: three guided meditations for this moment, plus daily tips. Free, no ads, works offline.
oracle.h1: The MeditaDream Oracle: three meditations for how you feel
oracle.lead: Not sure which meditation to pick? Tell the Oracle how you feel, in your own words. It shuffles the deck and turns over three cards: three guided meditations chosen for this exact moment.

p: The screen asks one question: “How are you feeling?” You answer the way you would talk to a friend: “I feel anxious before a big meeting”, “I can’t sleep, my mind is racing”, “I feel lonely tonight”.
The Oracle replies with a sentence, written letter by letter, then three cards appear. Tap a card to see the meditation and its length, and start the session.
ul: “Surprise me” draws three meditations at random.
Ask again as many times as you like.
Everything happens on your phone: nothing you write is sent anywhere.

p: “I feel anxious before a big meeting”: “I can feel everything rushing. Here are three ways to slow down, right now.” Then When Everything Moves Too Fast (4 min), Finding Your Confidence Before a Challenge (4 min) and Breathing with the Whole Body (13 min).

“I can’t sleep, my mind is racing”: “Sleep comes more easily when you stop chasing it. Let yourself be carried.” Then Drifting into Sleep (16 min), Sleep Journey (27 min) and Body Asleep, Mind Awake (24 min).
“I want to explore the stars”: “Craving somewhere else? Close your eyes, the journey starts here.” Then The Unknown Planet (17 min) and two longer journeys through the galaxy and the northern lights.
Suggestions can change from one day to the next, so you keep discovering new sessions.

sections.h2: Daily tips that sound like you
p: Below the cards, the Oracle offers tips for the day. The more you use the app, the more personal they get: they draw on your journals, the reflections you note after sessions, your guides and your favorites, sometimes in your own words.
At first, when it barely knows you, it picks from nearly a hundred tips across fourteen themes: breath, sleep, gratitude, body awareness and more.

Often the hardest part is not meditating, it is choosing. Faced with so many sessions, you scroll, hesitate, then put the phone down. The Oracle turns that choice into one simple question and three answers.
It is not fortune-telling: the Oracle matches your words to meditations. Drawing cards is simply a gentle way to welcome whatever comes up.

faq: Is the Oracle free?
Yes, like the whole app: no subscription, no ads, no account.
Do I need an internet connection?
Not for the cards or the tips, which are worked out on your phone. You only need a connection to download a session the first time.
What happens to what I write?
It stays on your phone. Nothing is sent or shared.
Does the Oracle replace a professional?
No. It suggests wellbeing meditations. If you are going through a hard time, talk to someone close to you or to a professional.

dragon.seo: Dragon Companion: A Meditation Pet That Grows With You
dragon.desc: Start with an egg, end with a cosmic dragon: your companion grows with every minute you meditate, across eleven stages on its own island. Free, no ads.
dragon.h1: Your dragon companion grows as you meditate
dragon.lead: In MeditaDream, every minute of meditation helps a companion grow: a dragon that hatches from an egg, moves to a new island as it matures, flies across a sky that follows your time of day, and talks to you with a dry sense of humor.

p: It grows with your total minutes of meditation, across eleven stages. The egg hatches after 10 minutes, the young dragon arrives after one hour of practice, the explorer at 300 minutes, the guardian at 1,000, and the cosmic dragon, the final stage, at 4,000 minutes.
ul: Dragon Egg: from the start
Hatchling Dragon: 10 minutes
Young Dragon: 60 minutes
Apprentice Dragon: 150 minutes
Adolescent Dragon: 225 minutes
Explorer Dragon: 300 minutes
Wayfarer Dragon: 500 minutes
Guardian Dragon: 1,000 minutes
Ancient Dragon: 2,000 minutes
Sage Dragon: 3,000 minutes
Cosmic Dragon: 4,000 minutes

p: Your dragon lives on an island floating in the sky, and the island evolves with it: a rock, a meadow, a sapling, a great tree, a waterfall, crystals, a temple, then a cosmic island.

It lands, moves around, meditates on the ground, then takes off for a flight. The sky follows your clock: daylight, sunset, a starry night with planets, an aurora on some nights, and visitors crossing the sky.

Meditate three days in a row and it is happy; seven days and it gets excited; fourteen and it turns wise. If it does not see you for three days it gets bored, and after a week it feels lonely. It celebrates every new stage and every stamp in your passport.

It talks to you too. On your first meeting: “Hello. I’m your spiritual dragon. I was supposed to be a tiger. There was an administrative issue.” After thirty days: “Thirty days. I may need to revise my theories about humans.”

As it grows, it earns items: a tiny lantern and a meditation cushion at the apprentice stage, an explorer’s hat, a compass and a passport bag at the explorer stage, a golden crown for the guardian, a halo for the sage, and a stardust cape for the cosmic dragon.
Because consistency matters more than length, and it feeds on small joys. Watching your dragon hatch, then grow, makes you want to come back tomorrow, even for five minutes.

faq: Does the dragon grow with short meditations?
Yes: it counts every minute, from 3-minute breaks to 40-minute journeys.
What happens if I stop for a few days?
It never shrinks and you lose nothing: it gets a little bored, then it is delighted when you come back.
Does the dragon cost anything?
No. Like the whole app, it is free, with no ads and no account.

journaux.seo: Dream Journal and 4 More Private Journals, Free
journaux.desc: A free dream journal, plus gratitude, emotion, signs and spiritual journals, all private and on your phone, inside a meditation app with no ads.
journaux.h1: A dream journal and four more: your private meditation journals
journaux.lead: MeditaDream does not stop when the session ends. Five journals help you keep track of what you live through: your dreams, your gratitude, your emotions, the signs you notice and your spiritual experiences.

sections.h2: Which journals are in the app?
ul: The dream journal, to write down dreams when you wake: their places, their characters, how they made you feel, and the ones that keep coming back.
The gratitude journal, to keep what did you good each day and what you take from it.
The emotion journal, to name what you feel, look for why, and watch how it changes.
The signs journal, for the coincidences that strike you, what you made of them at the time, and later on.
The spiritual journal, to record your inner experiences and the insights they leave behind.

sections.h2: How to keep a dream journal
ol: Keep your phone by the bed and open the dream journal as soon as you wake, before getting up.
Write down what remains, even a fragment: an image, a place, a feeling. Do not try to tell the whole story.
Add a word about how the dream made you feel.
Read your notes back every week: recurring dreams and insistent symbols show up on their own. It is also the first step toward lucid dreaming.

p: Every meditation you finish goes into your history, with its date and length. You can note your reflections there, across eight themes, and read them later to see how far you have come.

Everything stays on your phone: no account, no cloud, nothing is sent. Every entry earns you a point, just like every meditation, and the Oracle reads your journals right on your device to offer tips that sound like you.

faq: Are the journals private?
Yes. They stay on your phone, with no account and nothing sent.
How much do the journals cost?
Nothing. The journals, the meditations and the Oracle are free, with no subscription and no ads.
Can I keep a gratitude journal?
Yes, it is one of the five journals. The gratitude journal page explains how to keep it simple.

creer.seo: Write Your Own Guided Meditation, Free and Offline
creer.desc: Write your own guided meditation and hear it read aloud by a voice on your phone, pauses included, even offline. Free, no subscription, no ads.
creer.h1: My Meditations: write your own guided meditation
creer.lead: A line that helps you, a morning ritual, a visualization of your own: in My Meditations you write your own scripts, and the app reads them aloud, with the silences you choose.

sections.h2: How do you create your meditation?
ol: Give it a title, pick the language (English, French or Spanish) and the category to file it under.
Write your script, one sentence per line. The preview shows how many sentences you have and the estimated length.
Add silences: a line “3 sec” on its own between two sentences, or [10] for ten seconds. An empty line also lets the script breathe.
Press play: a voice on your phone reads your meditation, even offline.

sections.h2: An example to copy, then make your own
p: Here is a short morning meditation, written the way the app expects, one sentence per line:
ul: Settle in, back straight, shoulders soft.
3 sec
Feel the cool air coming in through your nose.
And the warmer air going out.
5 sec
Set one simple intention for today.
When you are ready, gently open your eyes.

p: Playback uses the voices installed on your phone. The “enhanced” or “premium” voices sound far more natural: the app shows you how to download them, on iPhone and Android, and they then appear in the list.
Your meditations are filed by category, just like the app’s own. You can edit or delete them at any time, and every session you play counts in your history and your points.

faq: Do I need a connection to play my meditation?
No: playback happens on your phone, even in airplane mode.
Can I write in French or Spanish?
Yes: choose the language of each meditation and the voice follows.
Are my scripts shared?
No. They stay on your phone.
